No inference to other tool domains, live deployment rates, or benign-task overblocking is supported.

item.title: A preprint reports measurable retention loss across multi-agent research handoffs
item.description: A September 15 preprint models how multi-agent decomposition affects the findings that survive to a root agent. It derives a yield relationship under a stated retention model and reports measurements from 600 production deep-research traces and 16,082 tool-result handoffs. The empirical estimates are author-reported and tied to one research scaffold.

item.title: A preprint reports faster 128K prefill with radius-adaptive sparse attention on Qwen models
item.description: A September 17 preprint proposes RBS-Attention, a training-free block selector that combines average key-block relevance with a radius-based rescue path intended to reduce false-negative pruning when a relevant token is diluted by unrelated tokens in the same block. For Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 at 128K on H100, the authors report 20.65× standalone prefill-attention, 11.92× vLLM prefill-attention and 5.97× end-to-end time-to-first-token speedups over dense execution in the same setup. On Qwen3-32B, they report 88.65 RULER accuracy versus 89.52 for dense attention. The paper includes actual-density selector comparisons and A100 memory measurements; in that implementation, temporary selector workspace is substantial. These are author-reported results from specific Qwen/GPU configurations, not an independent reproduction or a general serving-cost claim.

item.title: AMD researchers report a temporally stable one-step diffusion method for global illumination
item.description: An AMD research group describes a screen-space global-illumination method that uses a one-step latent diffusion model with scene and lighting conditions, plus a Temporal VAE decoder that reuses reprojected prior-frame information to reduce flicker. The authors train on synthetic Blender Cycles interior scenes and report improved PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and FovVideoVDP scores over the compared methods on their test scenes; a compact variant is also shown on real photographs using inverse-rendered inputs. The public technical article does not provide a measured runtime figure, and the research desk did not inspect or reproduce the full ECCV paper results.

item.title: Google publishes ARTEMIS, an open-source agent for Android automation and testing
item.description: Google’s public ARTEMIS repository provides natural-language Android automation through a reactive Flash profile and a slower plan-and-verify Pro profile, with CLI, Python SDK and MCP integrations for coding environments. The project describes accessibility-tree and OCR targeting with visual fallbacks, execution traces and history summaries. Its README claims 99%+ task completion on AndroidWorld’s 100+ multi-step tasks, but gives no model/version, per-task scores, trial counts or independent evaluation; this remains a first-party claim.

item.title: A preprint reports graph-format sensitivity and an adaptive reasoning scaffold for graph algorithms
item.description: A September 10 preprint introduces GT Bench, a synthetic evaluation of 24 classical graph problems across four textual/structural representations, and reports that the best input representation varies with graph and task structure. Its Graph Theory Agent (GTA) adds learned representation selection and plan/decompose scaffolding around a frozen executor. On the paper’s reported Phi-4 setting, accuracy rises from 53.5% to 69.1% on the easy split and 33.0% to 41.5% on the hard split; the authors also report transfer to other executors and benchmarks. These are author-reported results, not independently reproduced here. The abstract says 44 task–structure settings while Appendix C describes 43 reported settings.

item.title: Cactus releases Needle 3, a laddered quantized model for offline tool use on small devices
item.description: Cactus Compute released Needle 3 as a 2-bit, laddered model for local tool calling, structured extraction and text embeddings on devices ranging from phones to microcontrollers. The public model family spans 29–121 million parameters and 2–20 layer subnetworks, with the company describing 9–29 MB quantized variants and 8–29 MB package/model configurations. Cactus reports speed and benchmark advantages on mobile tool calling and structured extraction, but these comparisons come from its own tests and mix a CQ2 mobile binary, f16 baselines under vLLM and a hosted DeepSeek API. Independent matched accuracy, power, latency and real-use measurements remain open.

item.title: Language models use experimental records to predict research outcomes in fixed evaluations
item.description: In an October 8 preprint, Wang and colleagues report that language models prompted with records of prior experiments rank unseen research interventions more accurately in five fixed research environments and improve experiment selection in their evaluations. They also report gains in five multi-round OLMo3-100M simulations. The results are author-reported: some cross-environment uncertainty intervals include zero, transfer evidence is limited to autoregressive pretraining, and independent reproduction and deployed research value remain unestablished.
